# Network overview H5 fixture sources

The Debian 13 snapshots were read on 2026-11-22 as the enrolled installer account over pinned SSH. The existing fixture anonymizer replaces the hostname and MAC addresses. The MAC-derived alternate interface name uses its documentation MAC. The vault scrubber replaced a substring of the `available` heading and the fixture restores that fixed heading. The CPU samples retain the aggregate and per-core rows of the two `cat /proc/stat` responses, collected with a one-second pause. The other samples retain the bodies of `uname -a`, `free -m`, `ip -brief link`, `uptime`, `cat /sys/class/dmi/id/product_name`, `cat /proc/uptime` and `ip -s -j link show`.

FortiADC and Ruckus tests use existing anonymized captures under `real/fortiadc`, `fortiadc_adc_health`, `ruckus_wireless_path` and Admin's `fortiadc_adc_ha_state`. Their provenance files identify the commands and measured roles. Negative test copies edit those responses in memory to introduce duplicates, inconsistent counts, paging or a denied read.

`fortiadc/interface_counters/vendor` uses the documented RX/TX table layout from [FortiADC 7.4.9 diagnose netlink device](https://docs.fortinet.com/document/fortiadc/7.4.9/cli-reference/176977/diagnose-netlink-device), with reduced rows and example values for a five-port test. `fortiadc/vm_license/vendor` uses the documented successful response from [FortiADC 7.6.1 diagnose system vm](https://docs.fortinet.com/document/fortiadc/7.6.1/cli-reference/878940/diagnose-system-vm), with a neutral UUID, reduced fields and adjusted resource figures.
